newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 5.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Trade Union Congress of the Philippines, a coalition of labour groups, has filed for a 45-peso daily pay increase in the National Capital Region, Southern Tagalog and Central Luzon regions (MANILA CHRONICLE).

- Nobel Peace Prize winner Jose Ramos-Horta has apologised to President Fidel Ramos for causing him "personal discomfort" over his controversial plan to visit the Philippines during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. He told Ramos he wanted to visit the country on a "teaching assignment" in January 1997. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- Petron Corp is investing $3 billion for the construction of a new refinery and a petrochemical plant in the state-owned PNOC Petrochemical Development Corp complex in the northern Luzon island of Limay, Bataan (PHILIPPINE STAR).

- The Philippine House of Representatives passed on Monday on its third and final reading the national government's budget for 1997. House Bill 8033, which sets aside 476.2 billion pesos was approved with votes of 113 to 21. (BUSINESWORLD).
- The Department of Finance is not keen to shell out more funds to cover the 1.9 billion pesos duty drawback claims by the country's three oil refiners (BUSINESS DAILY).

- The Central Bank's director of economic research Diwa Gunigundo warned the Congress against legislating an increase in the daily minimum wage, saying such a move will only cause consumer prices, and subsequently, inflation rate, to go up (TODAY).
